typo.

Done, moved to a separate patch: [#80289]

[#80289]: https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/pldm/+/80289

Please be aware that this MR have unmerged libpldm dependencies, do not merge this commit before all the dependencies are merged.

Prerequisites: libpldm/[#80255]

[#80255]: https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/libpldm/+/80255
Whats the intent to collapse dropped enum types to a new one?

The new libpldm APIs alleviate the need for the libpldm consumer to do pointer arithmetic. The libpldm implementation resolves the component image in memory. There shouldn't be a need for the raw offset value.

Thanks for explanation! 😊
Mark as resolved.
Why are we doing this anyway? Why not use the struct provided by libpldm?
Removed enum and using struct provided by pldm.

descriptorDataPtr doesn't it needed to be freed? 
Not sure about the repo coding guidelines but wondering if it would be better to use unique_ptr and std::move as per need?

It's doing a [placement new](https://en.cppreference.com/w/cpp/language/new.html#Placement_new), but I don't think this use of it is correct. We don't want to construct an array in-place over the top of the data that's already populated? Just cast it as necessary?
Done, using static_cast directly.
You are dropping PackageParserV1, don't we want the code to be backwards compatible or the new additions will automatically take care of them?
Parsing of various format revisions now handled by libpldm directly.

Thanks for explanation! 😊
Mark as resolved.

@unive.tien.wiwynn@gmail.com With these changes, we might be creating multiple copies of the package . 
We should avoid this and ensure that only a single copy of the image is maintained, as was done in the previous implementation.
I think we should either use mmap here or load only header to memory while parsing the pacakge but with this component_image.ptr would be invalid
Acked, use the pointer provided from libpldm instead, which can avoid copies.

Why do we want to make an additional copy here ? 
I think we should switch back to file streaming where chunks of data were read on demand
Acked, use the pointer provided from libpldm instead, which can avoid copies.

Should we have a meson option to set the maximum package format
revision supported ? the default value can be 4 which could be DEFINE_PLDM_PACKAGE_FORMAT_PIN_FR04H.

Done.
```
option(
    'pldm-max-package-version',
    type: 'integer',
    value: '4',
    description: 'Maximum supported version of parsing pldm package',
)
```
